items.heading: README
items.code:
# dotfiles

used to config tmux, vim, yabai, etc

tmux source ~/.tmux.conf

`prefix + I` to fetch the tmux config.

`prefix + P` to start logging the tmux screen, `prefix + P` again to stop logging the tmux.


selecting text
`prefix + [`, then use `v` to select texts, and use `y` to copy selected texts.

items.heading: skhdrc
items.code:
# rotate layout clockwise
shift + alt - r : yabai -m space --rotate 270

# flip along y-axis
shift + alt - y : yabai -m space --mirror y-axis

# flip along x-axis
shift + alt - x : yabai -m space --mirror x-axis

# toggle window float
shift + alt - t : yabai -m window --toggle float --grid 4:4:1:1:2:2

# change window focus within space
alt - j : yabai -m window --focus south
alt - k : yabai -m window --focus north
alt - h : yabai -m window --focus west
alt - l : yabai -m window --focus east

#change focus between external displays (left and right)
alt - s: yabai -m display --focus west
alt - g: yabai -m display --focus east

# maximize a window
shift + alt - m : yabai -m window --toggle zoom-fullscreen

# balance out tree of windows (resize to occupy same area)
shift + alt - e : yabai -m space --balance

# swap windows
shift + alt - j : yabai -m window --swap south
shift + alt - k : yabai -m window --swap north
shift + alt - h : yabai -m window --swap west
shift + alt - l : yabai -m window --swap east

# move window and split
ctrl + alt - j : yabai -m window --warp south
ctrl + alt - k : yabai -m window --warp north
ctrl + alt - h : yabai -m window --warp west
ctrl + alt - l : yabai -m window --warp east

# move window to display left and right
shift + alt - s : yabai -m window --display west; yabai -m display --focus west;
shift + alt - g : yabai -m window --display east; yabai -m display --focus east;

#move window to prev and next space
shift + alt - p : yabai -m window --space prev;
shift + alt - n : yabai -m window --space next;

# move window to space #
shift + alt - 1 : yabai -m window --space 1;
shift + alt - 2 : yabai -m window --space 2;
shift + alt - 3 : yabai -m window --space 3;
shift + alt - 4 : yabai -m window --space 4;
shift + alt - 5 : yabai -m window --space 5;
shift + alt - 6 : yabai -m window --space 6;
shift + alt - 7 : yabai -m window --space 7;

# stop/start/restart yabai
ctrl + alt - q : yabai --stop-service
ctrl + alt - s : yabai --start-service
ctrl + alt - r : yabai --restart-service

items.heading: tmux.conf
items.code:
set -g mouse on

# plugins
set -g @plugin 'tmux-plugins/tmux-logging'
set -g @plugin 'tmux-plugins/tpm'
set -g @plugin 'tmux-plugins/tmux-sensible'
set -g @plugin 'dracula/tmux'
set -s default-terminal 'tmux-256color'

# dracula customizations
set -g @dracula-plugins "battery weather time"
set -g @dracula-show-powerline true
set -g @dracula-show-fahrenheit false
set -g @dracula-military-time true

run '~/.tmux/plugins/tpm/tpm'
set-option -g default-command "source ~/anaconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh; exec bash"

items.heading: yabairc
items.code:
yabai -m config layout bsp
yabai -m config window_placement second_child

# padding set to 12px
yabai -m config top_padding 12
yabai -m config bottom_padding 12
yabai -m config left_padding 12
yabai -m config right_padding 12
yabai -m config window_gap 12

# center mouse on window with focus
yabai -m config mouse_follows_focus on

# modifier for clicking and dragging with mouse
yabai -m config mouse_modifier alt
# set modifier + left-click drag to move window
yabai -m config mouse_action1 move
# set modifier + right-click drag to resize window
yabai -m config mouse_action2 resize


# when window is dropped in center of another window, swap them (on edges it will split it)
yabai -m mouse_drop_action swap

yabai -m rule --add app="^System Settings$" manage=off
yabai -m rule --add app="^Calculator$" manage=off
yabai -m rule --add app="^Karabiner-Elements$" manage=off

items.heading: Linux: Cache Git Credentials
items.note: Set Git to cache credentials in memory: Change the default cache timeout (in seconds):
items.code:
git config --global credential.helper cache

git config --global credential.helper 'cache --timeout=10800'

items.heading: macOS: Use Keychain for Git Credentials
items.note: Check if `osxkeychain` helper is installed: Set Git to use the `osxkeychain` helper:
items.code:
git credential-osxkeychain

git config --global credential.helper osxkeychain

items.heading: Reset Credentials for One Repository
items.note: Clear local credential helper so Git asks again for credentials:
items.code: git config --local credential.helper ""

items.heading: Reset Local Branch to Match Remote Branch
items.note: Use this when you want local files to exactly match `origin/v3`:
items.code:
git fetch origin
git reset --hard origin/v3
git clean -fd

items.heading: Merge a branch into `master`
items.note: 1. Make sure your local repo is up to date. 2. Switch to `master`. 3. Pull latest `master`. 4. Merge `v3` into `master`. 5. Push updated `master`. If Git opens Vim during merge commit, save and quit with:
items.code:
git fetch origin

git checkout master

git pull origin master

git merge v3

git push origin master

:wq

items.heading: Create a New Branch from Updated `master`
items.note: Push this branch after creating it.
items.code:
git switch master
git pull origin master
git switch -c v4-hiding-post

items.heading: Start `v7` from `v6`
items.code:
git checkout v6
git checkout -b v7

items.heading: Merge Completed `v7` Back to `v6`
items.code:
git checkout v6
git merge v7

items.heading: Merge `v6` into `master`
items.code:
git checkout master
git merge v6

items.heading: Update `v7` with Latest Changes from `v6`
items.note: If you pushed new commits to `v6` and want `v7` to match:
items.code:
git checkout v7
git merge v6

items.heading: Linux Commands
items.note: Give access of a folder to all users in Linux: Change name of all files in a directory using format: To find several files (in the example, PNG images) with specific name format and do whatever you want to do with them (in the example, convert them to JPG images), use the following example which uses command line tool find: Delete folders inside the path which name includes name_desired: Find 10 random files: Count the number of files in a folder: Count all files within a directory and its subdirectories: To see which processes are running:
items.code:
chmod -R a+rwx folder/

ls | cat -n | while read n f; do mv "$f" $(printf "%06d.png" "$n"); done

find . -type f -name "*.png" -not -name "*heatmaps.png" -print | while read f; do
  mogrify -format jpg $f
done

rm -rf `find . -maxdepth <num> -type d -name "<name_desired>"`

ls *.pdf | gshuf | head -10

ls <folder_path> | wc -l

find . -type f | wc -l
find ./ -type f -iname "*.JPEG" | wc -l

ps aux | grep python

items.heading: Example Slurm Batch Script
items.code:
#!/bin/bash

#SBATCH --job-name=extract_features

#SBATCH --nodes=1

#SBATCH --ntasks=1

#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=1

#SBATCH --mem=16G

#SBATCH --gres=gpu:1

#SBATCH --time=08:00:00

#SBATCH --output=extract_features_%j.log

#SBATCH --error=extract_features_%j.err

#SBATCH --partition=general

conda activate <env-name>

bash train.bash

items.heading: Another Slurm Script Example
items.code:
#!/bin/bash

#SBATCH --job-name=train_grpo_cot

#SBATCH --partition=general

#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=32

#SBATCH --mem=32G

#SBATCH --gres=gpu:2

#SBATCH --time=1-00:00:00

#SBATCH --output=train_grpo_cot_%j.log

#SBATCH --error=train_grpo_cot_%j.err

#SBATCH --nodelist=<node-name>

source ~/.bashrc

conda activate <env-name>

CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 python train_grpo.py --mode cot --cold_start_model_path <model-path>
